 CORAM:
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VIKAS MAHAJAN  OR % 13.03.2024 1.
The present petition has been filed under Section 439 CrPC seeking Regular Bail in connection with FIR No.685/2023 under Sections 419/420/468/471/120B/34 IPC registered at Police Station Shakarpur.

2. The case of the prosecution is that on 17th March, 2023, a complaint of Mr. Devender Singh was received at Police Station Shakarpur wherein he alleged that one Diptesh Chakraborty @ Rahul Singhania has cheated him in the name of Sky Overseas situated at D-30A, Shakarpur, Delhi on the pretext of enabling him to travel abroad.

3. During enquiry, six more complaints from the complainants, who are natives of Kerala, were received at Police Station Shakarpur against Sky Overseas regarding cheating of Rs.7.5 lakhs from each of such complainants.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 16/03/2024 at 01:16:38 4.
The learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner invites the attention of the Court to the FIR to contend that there is no allegation against the present petitioner.
The allegations are only against Diptesh Chakraborty.
None of the complainants stated to have ever interacted with the present petitioner or paid any amount to him.

sentences.text: 5. Further inviting attention of the Court to the Status Report dated 27th February, 2024, he submits that allegation against the petitioner is that there is a transfer of Rs.2,67,100/- made from the account of Sky Overseas, a concern of the co-accused Diptesh Chakraborty, to the bank account of the present petitioner.

6. He submits that the petitioner does not have any criminal record and the entire case is premised on documentary evidence and since charge sheet has already been filed, no recovery is required to be made from the petitioner.
7.
He, therefore, urges the Court to enlarge the petitioner.
8. Per contra the learned APP for the State has argued on the lines of the Status Report, which has been handed over in Court today and the same is taken on record.
9. She further submits that the investigation is still underway and there is possibility that supplementary charge sheet will be filed against the present petitioner.
10. A perusal of the FIR shows that there is no allegation made against the present petitioner.
The allegations made by the original complainant as well as subsequent complainants, who are natives of Kerala, are against the co-accused Diptesh Chakraborty.
11. A perusal of the Status Report dated 27th February, 2024 also shows This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 16/03/2024 at 01:16:38 that only an amount of Rs.2,67,100/- has been transferred from the concern of the co-accused Diptesh Chakraborty to the bank account of the present petitioner.
12. It is also not in dispute that the charge sheet has been filed, therefore, it appears that the petitioner is not further required for any investigation.
In any case, the case is based on documentary evidence which have already been collected during the investigation and made part of the charge sheet.
13. That apart, it is also not in dispute that the petitioner has clean antecedents and there are no cases registered against him.
14. Further the petitioner is stated to be permanent resident of Delhi, therefore, he does not appear to be a flight risk.

15. The petitioner is already in custody since 13th December, 2023, the charge sheet has already been filed but neither the charges have been framed nor the trial has commenced, therefore, the conclusion of trial is nowhere in sight and in the facts of the present case, the petitioner cannot be kept in custody for an indefinite period to await the outcome of the trial, more particularly when the Bail)

sentences.text: 16. In view of the above, this Court is of the opinion that the petitioner has made out a case for grant of regular bail.

Accordingly, the petitioner is enlarged on bail subject to his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 25,000/- and one surety bond of the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court/CMM/Duty Magistrate, further subject to the following conditions:-
a) Petitioner shall appear before the Court as and when the matter is taken up for hearing.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 16/03/2024 at 01:16:39 b) Petitioner shall provide mobile number to the IO concerned which shall be kept in working condition at all times and he shall not change the mobile number without prior intimation to the Investigating Officer concerned.
c) Petitioner shall not indulge in any criminal activity and shall not communicate with or come in contact with the witnesses.
d) Since investigation is stated to be pending against the present petitioner, he is directed to join the investigation as and when he is called upon by the Investigating Officer concerned.
17. The petition along with pending applications stands disposed of.
18. It is made clear that nothing stated above is to be construed as an expression of opinion on the merits of the case.
19. Copy of the order be forwarded to the concerned Jail Superintendent for necessary compliance and information.

20. Order dasti under signatures of the Court Master.
21.
Order be uploaded on the website of this Court.
VIKAS MAHAJAN, J MARCH 13, 2024 ak
